title: Instant Pot Southern Chicken & Flat Dumplings
dek: Tender chicken and hand-cut flat dumplings simmer in a creamy thyme broth, with pressure cooking handling the chicken before the dumplings finish uncovered.
image_alt: Southern chicken and flat dumplings in a pale creamy broth served in a wide white bowl
ingredients: 1 cup all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
1/3 cup whole milk, plus 1/2 cup for finishing

instructions.name: Mix and rest the dough
instructions.text: Whisk flour, baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cut in cold butter until pea-size crumbs form, stir in 1/3 cup milk, and knead just until smooth. Cover and rest 20 minutes while the chicken cooks.

instructions.name: Brown the chicken
instructions.text: Season chicken with 1 teaspoon salt and pepper. Select Sauté High on a 6-quart electric pressure cooker, add oil and brown chicken in two batches for about 3 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate.

instructions.name: Build a thin, clean base
instructions.text: Reduce Sauté to Normal. Cook onion, celery and carrots for 4 minutes; add garlic and thyme for 30 seconds. Pour in 1 cup broth and scrape until the heating plate is completely smooth. Add the remaining 3 cups broth and bay leaf, then return chicken without adding milk or cream.

instructions.name: Pressure-cook and release
instructions.text: Lock the lid and cook on High Pressure for 8 minutes; allow about 12 minutes to reach pressure. Let pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then vent the remainder in short controlled pulses. Open only after the float valve drops.

instructions.name: Verify and shred
instructions.text: Check several thigh pieces in the thickest part for at least 165°F. Transfer chicken to a clean board, shred it and discard the bay leaf. If any piece is below 165°F, return it to the simmering broth until it reaches the safe temperature.

instructions.name: Roll and cut flat dumplings
instructions.text: On a lightly floured surface roll dough about 1/8 inch thick and cut into 1-by-2-inch strips. Select Sauté Low and bring the broth to a gentle simmer. Drop in dumplings one at a time, stirring carefully so they do not clump.

instructions.name: Simmer and finish
instructions.text: Simmer uncovered 8 to 10 minutes, stirring along the base often, until dumplings are tender with no raw flour center. Return chicken, stir in 1/2 cup milk and cream, and heat gently to 165°F without a hard boil. Finish with parsley.

instructions.name: Serve mild-first
instructions.text: Taste and add up to the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt. Ladle into bowls and offer hot sauce separately so the shared pot stays family-friendly.

why_it_works: Four cups of thin broth contact a fully deglazed base, while dairy stays out until after pressure to reduce scorching risk.
Pressure cooking makes the chicken tender quickly, but uncovered simmering preserves the flat dumplings' distinct, noodle-like texture.
A short dough rest hydrates the flour so thin dumplings roll cleanly without becoming tough from extra kneading.
swaps: Use bone-in thighs and pressure-cook 10 minutes, then remove bones and verify 165°F before shredding.
Replace heavy cream with additional whole milk for a lighter broth; do not add either dairy ingredient before pressure cooking.
Use 12 ounces refrigerated flat egg noodles for a shortcut, simmering according to package timing instead of making dumplings.
storage: Cool in shallow containers within 2 hours and refrigerate up to 4 days. Freeze up to 2 months, although dumplings soften after thawing. Reheat gently to 165°F with extra broth or milk; stir often so the thickened soup does not scorch.
notes: Total time includes about 12 minutes to pressurize, the 8-minute cycle, a 10-minute natural release and the post-pressure dumpling simmer.
Follow the exact model manual for minimum liquid, maximum fill, locking and venting; never force the lid.
Do not pressure-cook the flour dumplings or dairy in this version; both are added after the lid comes off.
Keep the pot below the maximum-fill line and do not double this recipe in a 6-quart cooker.

faqs.q: Why are the dumplings cooked after pressure releases?
faqs.a: Thin flour strips need only a gentle simmer. Adding them afterward prevents them from dissolving or sticking to the heating plate during pressure cooking.

faqs.q: How do I know flat dumplings are done?
faqs.a: Cut the thickest strip: it should be tender and opaque throughout, without a chalky or gummy flour center.
Yes. Use breasts of similar thickness, keep the 8-minute cycle, and check every piece for 165°F before shredding so lean meat is not overcooked.

title: Instant Pot Ecuadorian-Style Locro de Queso with Avocado
dek: Starchy potatoes create their own silky body in this mild Ecuadorian cheese soup, finished after pressure with queso fresco, milk, avocado and cilantro.
image_alt: Golden Ecuadorian locro de queso potato soup topped with avocado, white cheese and cilantro in a rustic bowl
ingredients: 1 tsp ground annatto or sweet paprika
3 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch chunks
8 oz queso fresco, crumbled and divided
Sliced jalapeño or ají sauce, optional for serving

instructions.name: Sweat the aromatics
instructions.text: Select Sauté Normal on a 6-quart electric pressure cooker. Melt butter and cook onion 5 minutes until soft. Add garlic, cumin and annatto for 30 seconds without browning.

instructions.name: Deglaze and layer
instructions.text: Pour in 1 cup broth and scrape until the heating plate is completely smooth. Add remaining broth, potatoes and 1 teaspoon salt. Stir once and keep the contents below the maximum-fill line; do not add milk or cheese before pressure.

instructions.name: Pressure-cook
instructions.text: Lock the lid and cook on High Pressure for 7 minutes; allow about 12 minutes to reach pressure. Use a controlled quick release in short pulses, pausing immediately if starchy liquid sputters. Open only after the float valve drops.

instructions.name: Create the creamy body
instructions.text: Mash roughly one-third of the potatoes against the pot wall, leaving the rest chunky. Select Sauté Low and stir often across the base for 2 to 3 minutes.

instructions.name: Add dairy safely
instructions.text: Stir in milk and 6 ounces queso fresco. Heat gently, stirring, until the soup reaches 165°F and the cheese softens; do not boil hard. Add up to the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt after tasting the cheese.

instructions.name: Finish the bowls
instructions.text: Ladle into warm bowls and top with the remaining queso fresco, avocado and cilantro. Serve lime, jalapeño and ají sauce at the table so the shared soup remains mild.

why_it_works: A full four cups of thin broth sit against a deglazed base, while burn-prone milk and cheese wait until pressure has fallen.
Yukon Gold potatoes both hold tender chunks and release enough starch when mashed to thicken the soup without flour.
Cool avocado, fresh cilantro and lime balance the rich potato-and-cheese base and mirror the visible finished presentation.
swaps: Use russet potatoes for an even thicker soup, mashing less because they release more starch.
Replace queso fresco with farmer cheese or a mild feta; reduce added salt if the substitute is briny.
Use lactose-free whole milk and a suitable mild cheese if needed; plant milk changes the traditional dairy flavor.
storage: Refrigerate the soup without avocado in shallow containers for up to 4 days; freeze up to 2 months before adding dairy for the smoothest texture. Reheat gently to 165°F, stirring often and thinning with broth. Add fresh avocado only when serving.
notes: Total time includes about 12 minutes to pressurize, the 7-minute cycle, controlled release and post-pressure finishing.
Follow the exact model manual for minimum liquid, maximum fill and venting; an 8-quart cooker may require more thin liquid.
Potatoes are starchy, so vent in brief pulses and stop if foam or liquid emerges from the valve.
The optional chile is intentionally served at the table rather than cooked into the family pot.

faqs.q: Why is dairy added after pressure cooking?
faqs.a: Milk and cheese can scorch on the hot base or separate under pressure. Adding them during the gentle finishing stage gives a smoother soup.

faqs.q: Can I make locro de queso ahead?
faqs.a: Yes. Prepare through the dairy finish, cool promptly and refrigerate. Reheat slowly and add avocado, cilantro and lime just before serving.

faqs.q: What if the soup is thinner than I want?
faqs.a: Mash more potatoes and simmer on Sauté Low for a few minutes, stirring across the base. Avoid adding raw flour directly to the pot.

title: Polish Potato & Cheese Pierogi
dek: Tender handmade pierogi wrap a savory potato, farmer-cheese and onion filling, with reliable dough cues, freezer directions and two finishing options.
image_alt: Bowl of boiled Polish pierogi filled with potato, cheese and onion
ingredients: 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
1 lb russet potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
8 oz farmer cheese or well-drained twaróg
Sour cream and chopped chives, optional for serving

instructions.name: Make the supple dough
instructions.text: Whisk flour with 1/2 teaspoon salt. Add egg, warm water and oil; mix, then knead 6 to 8 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and rest 30 minutes so rolling requires less force.

instructions.name: Cook and dry the potatoes
instructions.text: Cover potatoes with cold salted water, bring to a boil and simmer 12 to 15 minutes until easily pierced. Drain thoroughly, return to the warm pan for 1 minute and mash smooth.

instructions.name: Build the filling
instructions.text: Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet over medium and cook half the onion 8 to 10 minutes until golden. Mix with warm potato, farmer cheese, remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and pepper. Cool completely.

instructions.name: Roll and fill
instructions.text: Divide dough in two, keeping one half covered. Roll the other 1/16 inch thick and cut 3-inch rounds. Place 1 tablespoon filling in each, fold into half-moons and firmly pinch out air. Keep finished pierogi covered and repeat.

instructions.name: Boil in batches
instructions.text: Bring a wide pot of salted water to a gentle boil. Cook 8 to 10 pierogi at a time; once they float, simmer 2 minutes more. Lift with a slotted spoon and coat lightly with 1 tablespoon butter.

instructions.name: Choose the finish
instructions.text: Serve the boiled pierogi as pictured, or melt the remaining butter in a skillet and cook the remaining onion until golden, then sear pierogi 2 minutes per side. Serve sour cream and chives separately.

why_it_works: Drying the drained potatoes prevents a wet filling that would weaken the dough seams.
A full 30-minute dough rest relaxes gluten, allowing thin wrappers without spring-back.
Cooking at a gentle boil protects sealed edges while the two-minute float time heats the filling through.
swaps: Use ricotta only after draining it overnight and mixing with a little crumbled feta to approximate farmer cheese's dry tang.
Replace half the onion with finely sliced leek for a sweeter filling.
Freeze shaped pierogi on a tray, then bag them and boil from frozen, adding 2 to 3 minutes.
storage: Refrigerate cooked pierogi up to 4 days or freeze uncooked pierogi in a single layer before transferring to a freezer bag for up to 3 months. Reheat refrigerated pierogi in a buttered skillet until the filling reaches 165°F.
notes: Keep filling cool and wrappers covered; warm filling or dry edges make seals unreliable.
Do not overfill. A clean 1/4-inch rim is easier to seal than a stretched, floury edge.
Farmer cheese varies in salt, so taste the cooled filling before adding the final seasoning.
Total time includes the dough rest and filling cool-down.

faqs.q: Why do my pierogi open in the water?
faqs.a: Trapped air, filling on the rim or dried dough can break the seam. Press out air, keep the edge clean and pinch firmly before boiling.

faqs.q: Can I make the dough without egg?
faqs.a: Yes. Replace the egg with about 3 tablespoons additional warm water, adding it gradually until the dough is supple but not sticky.

faqs.q: Should pierogi be boiled or fried?
faqs.a: They must be boiled to cook the dough. Pan-frying afterward is optional and adds browned edges; the licensed hero image shows the boiled version.

title: Sichuan-Style Mapo Tofu with Pork & Steamed Rice
dek: Silken tofu and a modest amount of pork simmer in a glossy chile-bean sauce, with Sichuan pepper and extra heat added to taste at the table.
image_alt: Sichuan-style mapo tofu with cubes of tofu, ground pork, chile oil, scallions and Sichuan pepper
ingredients: 14 oz soft tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
2 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp cool water
1/2 tsp toasted ground Sichuan pepper, plus more for serving

instructions.name: Steam the rice
instructions.text: Combine rinsed rice and water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce to low and cook 15 minutes. Remove from heat and rest covered 10 minutes.

instructions.name: Warm the tofu
instructions.text: Slide tofu into barely simmering salted water for 2 minutes, then drain carefully. This warms and firms the cubes so they are less likely to break in the sauce.

instructions.name: Brown the pork
instructions.text: Heat a wok or wide skillet over medium-high. Add oil and pork; cook 4 to 5 minutes, breaking it into small pieces, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F.

instructions.name: Bloom the seasonings
instructions.text: Reduce heat to medium. Stir in doubanjiang and black beans for 1 minute until the oil turns red, then add garlic and ginger for 30 seconds. Keep this base mild; chile oil stays at the table.

instructions.name: Simmer the tofu
instructions.text: Add broth, soy sauce and sugar and bring to a gentle simmer. Slide in tofu and simmer 5 minutes, nudging rather than stirring so the cubes remain distinct.

instructions.name: Thicken in two stages
instructions.text: Stir the cornstarch slurry again. Drizzle in half, gently shake the pan and simmer 30 seconds; add only enough of the remainder for a sauce that lightly clings to the tofu.

instructions.name: Finish and serve
instructions.text: Remove from heat and add sesame oil, scallions and 1/2 teaspoon Sichuan pepper. Spoon over rice and offer extra pepper and chile oil separately.

why_it_works: Briefly warming soft tofu firms its surface and reduces breakage without changing its custardy center.
Cooking doubanjiang in oil releases its red color and savory aroma before thin broth dilutes the base.
Adding slurry gradually avoids the heavy, gluey sauce that can result from using all the starch at once.
swaps: Use medium tofu for easier handling; the finished dish will be slightly firmer.
Replace pork with ground turkey and verify 165°F, or minced mushrooms for a meatless variation.
If fermented black beans are unavailable, omit them and add 1 teaspoon additional doubanjiang after tasting.
storage: Refrigerate mapo tofu and rice separately within 2 hours for up to 3 days. Reheat the tofu gently to 165°F, adding broth if the sauce tightens. Reheat rice to 165°F and discard rice left at room temperature longer than 2 hours.
notes: Doubanjiang brands vary in heat and salt; choose a mild version and taste before adding soy sauce.
Sichuan pepper creates citrusy tingling rather than chile heat; serve extra at the table for individual control.
Do not vigorously stir once tofu enters the pan. Shake or fold with a broad spatula.
The licensed image clearly shows cubed tofu, red chile-bean oil, pork and scallion.

faqs.q: Is mapo tofu always very spicy?
faqs.a: It is traditionally bold, but heat varies. This family-oriented version uses mild doubanjiang and moves additional chile oil to the table.
Very soft tofu breaks if stirred. Warm it briefly, drain carefully and move the pan rather than repeatedly running a spoon through the cubes.

faqs.q: Can I make it without pork?
faqs.a: Yes. Finely chopped shiitakes provide savory texture; use vegetable broth and confirm your doubanjiang is vegetarian.

title: Mexican-Style Tres Leches Cake with Whipped Cream
dek: An airy sponge absorbs a balanced three-milk soak without collapsing, then chills overnight beneath a light whipped-cream finish.
image_alt: Square slice of pale golden tres leches cake with a thick white whipped-cream topping on a plate
ingredients: 3/4 cup heavy cream for the soak
1 1/2 cups cold heavy cream for topping
1/2 tsp ground cinnamon, optional for serving

instructions.name: Prepare the pan
instructions.text: Heat oven to 350°F. Butter the bottom of a 9-by-13-inch metal pan and line it with parchment, leaving the sides ungreased so the sponge can climb.

instructions.name: Whip the yolk batter
instructions.text: Whisk flour, baking powder and salt. Beat yolks with 3/4 cup sugar for 3 minutes until thick and pale; mix in 1/3 cup milk and 1 teaspoon vanilla, then fold in the dry ingredients.

instructions.name: Fold in the whites
instructions.text: With clean beaters, whip egg whites to soft peaks. Gradually add remaining 1/4 cup sugar and beat to glossy medium peaks. Fold into yolk batter in three additions without deflating it.

instructions.name: Bake to a dry crumb
instructions.text: Spread batter evenly and bake 25 to 28 minutes until golden, springy and 200 to 205°F in the center. Cool in the pan 20 minutes, remove parchment and return cake to the pan.

instructions.name: Soak gradually
instructions.text: Whisk evaporated milk, condensed milk, 3/4 cup cream and remaining vanilla. Poke the warm cake every inch with a skewer. Pour the soak over in three passes, waiting 5 minutes between additions.

instructions.name: Chill thoroughly
instructions.text: Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, until the milk is evenly absorbed and the cake is cold throughout.

instructions.name: Top and serve
instructions.text: Whip 1 1/2 cups cold cream with confectioners' sugar to medium peaks. Spread over the cake, dust lightly with cinnamon if desired and cut into 12 cold squares.

why_it_works: Separately whipped whites create an open sponge able to absorb substantial liquid without turning leaden.
Pouring the milk mixture in stages distributes it more evenly than flooding the center all at once.
A long cold rest lets the crumb hydrate completely and gives the whipped topping a stable base.
swaps: Use lactose-free evaporated milk, condensed milk and cream in the same quantities if available.
Add 1 teaspoon finely grated orange zest to the milk soak for a citrus variation.
Top servings with fresh strawberries, but store the berries separately so they do not weep into the cream.
storage: Keep the covered cake refrigerated and serve within 4 days. Return it to the refrigerator within 2 hours because the milk soak and whipped cream are perishable. Freezing is not recommended after soaking because the dairy can separate.
notes: Total time includes a four-hour minimum chill; overnight chilling gives the cleanest slices.
Use clean, grease-free equipment for the egg whites or they may not whip to full volume.
The cake should be moist with a little milk at the plate, not floating in an unabsorbed pool.
Eggs are fully cooked when the center of the sponge reaches 200 to 205°F.

faqs.q: Why did my tres leches cake become soggy?
faqs.a: An underbaked or deflated sponge cannot hold the soak. Bake to at least 200°F and fold the whites gently so the crumb remains open.

faqs.q: Can I serve it the same day?
faqs.a: Yes after at least four hours of chilling, but an overnight rest distributes the milk more evenly and makes neater slices.

faqs.q: Why leave the pan sides ungreased?
faqs.a: The foam-based batter grips the sides as it rises. Greasing only the lined bottom supports a taller, more absorbent sponge.
